```{=html}
  <div class="project-text">
    <h2>Background</h2>

    <p>Underwater remotely operated vehicles provide a cost-effective solution for retrieving environmental data in aquatic settings. This project was motivated by the need to design and deploy a functional ROV capable of measuring temperature and pressure signals in lake environments.</p>

    <p>The goal was to develop a system that could reliably collect sensor data using the MCP9701 thermistor and MPX5700ASX pressure gauge, and process output voltages for analysis in LabVIEW. The ROV needed to be robust enough for real lake deployment while remaining buildable within the constraints of a course project.</p>
  </div>

</div>

<p>To bring the system together, I assembled a PCB containing the MCP6002 OpAmp to condition and return output voltages from the sensors. Each circuit was carefully soldered and tested using an oscilloscope and DMM to verify signal integrity before deployment. The output voltages were then modeled and analyzed in LabVIEW, allowing us to interpret the sensor readings and validate the performance of the system in real aquatic conditions.</p>
```
